$comment: Accepted dependency advisories. Enforced by scripts/audit.ts (`bun run audit`), which
fails CI on any high/critical advisory NOT listed here, on any entry past its reviewBy
date, on any entry no longer present in the graph, and on any `no-fix-available` entry
that upstream has since fixed — including a fix published under a renamed package.
This replaced a bare `bun audit --ignore=GHSA-...` flag, which had no exit condition and
spent two months suppressing an advisory that had already been fixed upstream.
no-fix-available  upstream has published no fixed release. Re-verified against the
GitHub advisory API on every run and fails the moment one appears,
including a fix shipped under a renamed successor package.
backlog           a fix exists; the upgrade is queued. Bounded by reviewBy.
not-exploitable   only reachable through a code path this repo does not use.
pinned            the vulnerable version is deliberately pinned and the pin is load-bearing.

accepted.title: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
accepted.reason: Reached only through metro/expo, which use image-size at BUILD time to read asset dimensions; the JXL/HEIF infinite loop needs a hostile image inside our own repo, and no image-size code ships in the app binary. No fix exists to take: every published version is vulnerable (<=2.0.2 covers latest 2.0.2, first_patched_version null on both advisories), and npm audit fixAvailable points at expo@53.0.27 — a four-major DOWNGRADE from our ~57.0.0, not a fix. The gate re-verifies this against the advisory API on every run and fails the moment image-size or a renamed successor ships a patch.

accepted.title: image-size: ICNS parser allows denial of service through an infinite loop
accepted.reason: Same package, parser and reachability as GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq: build-time metro/expo asset sizing, nothing shipped in the app binary, triggered only by a hostile ICNS file in our own repo. No fix exists to take: latest image-size 2.0.2 is itself in range and both advisories report first_patched_version null, while npm audit fixAvailable suggests expo@53.0.27, a four-major downgrade from our ~57.0.0. The gate re-verifies against the advisory API on every run and fails as soon as a real patch appears.
